266.h: Federal University, Gusau (FUGUS) was one of twelve new federal universities proposed in 2010. Nine were opened in February 2011; Gusau was among the remaining three, established in 2013 under President Goodluck Jonathan. Academic activities started in September 2015.
266.a: The university started with three faculties: Humanities and Education, Management and Social Sciences, and Science. Its library, established in 2014, opened with the university in a single classroom seating 50 readers. Donations from publishers, the Emeka Offor Foundation and others, followed by Tertiary Education Trust Fund grants from 2016, built its collection to about 298,000 books and journals, and it now serves four faculties with seventeen departments, with an e-library section.
266.c: It is located in Gusau, the capital of Zamfara State.

327.h: Summit University, Offa is a private university founded in 2015 by the Ansar-Ud-Deen Society of Nigeria, a Muslim organisation devoted to education. It was one of ten private universities licensed in Nigeria that year, and one of the few private universities in Kwara State. It began full operations in November 2016 with 500 students, under its founding vice-chancellor, Professor Hussein Oloyede.
327.a: The university is organised into colleges. Natural and Applied Sciences covers biological sciences, chemical sciences and computer science. Management and Social Sciences offers mass communication, political science, economics, and management and accounting, and a humanities college teaches English and literary studies and Arabic and Islamic studies. Scholarships are available, among them the General Sawyer Scholarship.
327.c: It is located in Offa, Kwara State, in north-central Nigeria.

264.h: Federal University, Dutsin-Ma (FUDMA) was founded in February 2011 by the administration of President Goodluck Jonathan, as one of the nine new federal universities created that year. It began full operations in 2012.
264.a: FUDMA's Faculty of Agriculture covers agricultural economics, animal science, crop science, fisheries and aquaculture, forestry and wildlife, and soil science. Its Faculty of Engineering and Technology offers agricultural and bio-resources, chemical, civil, electrical and electronic, mechanical and mechatronics engineering. There are also faculties of Arts and Social Sciences, Computing, Education (with combined subject degrees, early childhood, primary and special education), Environmental Sciences (architecture, building, quantity surveying and urban planning) and Management Sciences.
264.c: It is located in Dutsin-Ma, Katsina State, in north-western Nigeria.

240.h: Confluence University of Science and Technology (CUSTECH) is a public technical university owned by the Kogi State Government. The Kogi State House of Assembly passed the bill to establish it on 19 August 2020. Its name refers to Kogi State's position at the confluence of the Niger and Benue rivers. In May 2024 students were abducted from the campus while preparing for first-semester examinations.
240.a: In 2024 the National Universities Commission gave full approval to all its courses, including medicine and law, and in February 2024 approved anatomy, physiology and related medical courses. In December 2024 a state law converted the Reference Hospital, Okene, into the CUSTECH Teaching Hospital. The library opened in March 2021 with 600 volumes.
240.c: The campus is at Osara in Kogi State.
